ogDesc: A detailed day-by-day Koh Samet plan: which beaches to swim at, where to snorkel, how to do the island boat loop, with real costs.
intro: Koh Samet is one of the closest islands to Bangkok. Drive to Ban Phe, hop on a boat for about 40 minutes, and you're on white sand with clear water. This plan covers everything: a stay at the popular Sai Kaew Beach, quieter swims at Ao Phrao, a snorkeling boat loop around the island, and the walk up to the Khao Laem Ya viewpoint. Written like a friend filling you in, with the boat fares and park fees you'll actually pay.

blocks.html: The appeal of Koh Samet is that it's easy to reach and the sea really is lovely. The east-coast beaches like Sai Kaew, Ao Phai and Ao Wong Duean are fine white sand you can walk between, while the west side has Ao Phrao, which is quieter with the best sunsets. The island sits inside Khao Laem Ya–Mu Ko Samet National Park, so there's a fee checkpoint before you go in. This 3-day, 2-night plan keeps the first day relaxed for arrival, a full-day snorkeling boat loop on day two, and the viewpoint walk on day three before heading home.

blocks.text: Before you go — boat fares, park fees, what to prep

items: Getting to Ban Phe — minivans from Ekkamai run all day, around ฿200–250 each way, taking roughly 3–4 hours to Ban Phe pier.
Crossing to the island — the Ban Phe–Na Dan (Sai Kaew Beach) passenger ferry is around ฿100 round trip and takes about 40 minutes. First boat at 8:00 a.m., last around 6:00 p.m.
Speedboat — a charter runs roughly ฿1,500–2,600 per trip depending on boat size and group, faster and available anytime. Worth it for larger groups or late arrivals.
National park fee — ฿40 for Thai adults, ฿20 for children (฿200 for foreign adults), collected at the checkpoint on the island. Keep the receipt in case you're checked again.
Cash — ATMs on the island are few and lines are long, so withdraw enough on the Ban Phe side before you cross.

blocks.title: Booking your stay
blocks.html: Places near Sai Kaew Beach are lively and close to the pier, so they're easy to reach, but it gets noisy at night. If you want quiet, pick the Ao Wong Duean or Ao Phrao side instead. Rooms fill fast on weekends and long holidays, so book ahead.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Arrive and hit Sai Kaew Beach

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Arrive, save your energy for a cool swim

items.activity: Leave Bangkok, take an Ekkamai minivan to Ban Phe
items.note: Leave a bit early to catch a mid-morning boat and get a full day in the water.

items.activity: Arrive at Ban Phe pier, withdraw cash, buy ferry tickets
items.note: The Ban Phe side has dried-seafood souvenir shops you can hit on the way back.

items.activity: Take the ferry across to Na Dan pier, Koh Samet
items.note: About a 40-minute ride. Pay the national park fee at the checkpoint on the island.

items.activity: Check in, lunch by Sai Kaew Beach
items.note: Beachfront spots serve seafood and made-to-order dishes — tourist prices, but you get the setting.

items.activity: Swim at Sai Kaew Beach: fine white sand, shallow water
items.note: This is the busiest beach on the island. Clear water, few rocks, good for swimming and watersports.

items.activity: Walk the shore to Ao Phai and Ao Phutsa for the evening light
items.note: The east-coast beaches connect, and each bay gets quieter as you go.

items.activity: Grilled-seafood dinner by the sea
items.note: Several spots have fire shows in the evening, so you can settle in for a long meal.

blocks.html: The highlight of this plan is day two: a boat around Koh Samet and the small nearby islands to snorkel over shallow coral. Popular trips come in half-day and full-day versions, stopping at several spots to swim, see coral, and pull up on a quiet beach for lunch.

items.activity: Breakfast, get ready for the island boat tour
items.note: Book through your hotel or a beach shop — there are both longtail boats and speedboats.

items.activity: Set off, first snorkel stop around Ao Kiu and Ao Thapthim
items.note: Ao Kiu has clear water and shallow coral, good for beginners. Mask-and-snorkel rental runs about ฿100–200.

items.activity: Stop at a quiet bay on the south side to swim and shoot photos
items.note: South-side bays like Ao Wai and Ao Karang are uncrowded with calm water.

items.activity: Pull up for lunch on the beach
items.note: Full-day tours usually include a boxed lunch or stop so you can order food on the beach.

items.activity: Second snorkel stop for coral and fish
items.note: Bigger loops may swing by nearby islands like Koh Kudi or Koh Talu.

items.activity: Loop back to the Ao Phrao side to wait for sunset
items.note: Ao Phrao is on the west side, the best sunset spot on the island.

items.activity: Back to your room, shower, find dinner
items.note: After a full day in the sun, take it easy tonight.

blocks.title: About the tides
blocks.html: Underwater visibility depends on the weather and currents — some days are murkier than usual. Ask the boatman where the water's clear that day, and don't expect Andaman-clear water every time. Honestly, Koh Samet is more about its sandy beaches than its reefs.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Khao Laem Ya viewpoint before heading home

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Catch the view, grab souvenirs, head back

items.activity: Breakfast, pack up, check out
items.note: Ask your hotel how late you can leave bags so you can keep exploring without worry.

items.activity: Walk the nature trail up to the viewpoint
items.note: The trail up and down is about 1.5 km, ending at a Sky Walk with 360-degree views. Sneakers make the walk easier.

items.activity: Come down for one last swim at a beach near your room
items.note: Catch the clear morning sea while there are still few people around.

items.activity: Lunch, grab your bags, walk to the pier
items.note: Leave time for the boat — the queue gets long on holiday afternoons.

items.activity: Ferry back to Ban Phe, stop for dried-seafood souvenirs
items.note: Ban Phe is known for shrimp paste, dried squid and dried shrimp — easy souvenirs to take home.

items.activity: Catch the minivan back to Bangkok
items.note: You'll reach Bangkok around evening — a tidy end to the trip without overdoing it.

blocks.text: Pick the beach that fits your style

items.name: Sai Kaew Beach
items.blurb: The popular beach on the north side: fine white sand, shallow easy water, busy all day, with plenty of restaurants and watersports. Good for friends and families who want convenience.

items.name: Ao Wong Duean
items.blurb: A crescent-shaped bay on the east side with pretty sand, resorts and restaurants, a touch quieter than Sai Kaew. Good for couples or anyone wanting a more laid-back vibe than the main beach.

items.name: Ao Phrao
items.blurb: On the west side: quiet, private, and the best sunset spot on the island. Good for getting away from the crowds.

items.name: Ao Kiu & Ao Thapthim
items.blurb: Small bays on the south side with clear water, shallow coral and few people. Good for a snorkel stop on the island boat loop.

items: Round-trip island ferry — around ฿100 (passenger ferry), or split a speedboat charter
Island snorkeling tour — around ฿400–800 depending on half-day/full-day and number of stops
2 nights' lodging — from a few hundred up to a few thousand THB per night, depending on the beach and season
Food — beachfront seafood runs a few hundred per meal, budget ฿400–700 a day

blocks.title: The best time to go
blocks.html: Koh Samet is good almost year-round since it's on the Gulf side and gets less rain than many islands. The clearest water and calmest seas tend to run roughly November through April. Skip the long holidays unless you don't mind crowds and pricier rooms.

faq.q: How many nights should I spend on Koh Samet?
faq.a: Two nights is just right: beach time on day one, a full-day snorkeling boat loop on day two, and the viewpoint before you leave on day three. If you're really short on time, a day trip works, but it'll feel rushed and you'll miss the sunset.

faq.q: Where's the best snorkeling on Koh Samet?
faq.a: The popular spots are Ao Kiu and Ao Thapthim on the south side: clear water, shallow coral, good for beginners. Most people go with an island boat tour that hits several stops. Snorkel gear rental runs about 100–200 THB.

faq.q: How much is the boat to Koh Samet?
faq.a: The passenger ferry from Ban Phe to Sai Kaew Beach is around 100 THB round trip and takes about 40 minutes. A speedboat charter runs roughly 1,500–2,600 THB per trip, depending on boat size and group.

faq.q: Do I have to pay the national park fee?
faq.a: Yes, because Koh Samet sits inside Khao Laem Ya–Mu Ko Samet National Park. It's 40 THB for Thai adults and 20 THB for children, collected at the checkpoint on the island. Keep your receipt.

faq.q: Which beach is best for families with kids?
faq.a: Sai Kaew Beach is the best bet: shallow water, fine sand, few rocks, plus restaurants and lodging near the pier, so it's easy to get to. If you want it quieter, Ao Wong Duean is a good pick.
